intro: Pest control builds time management, problem solving and safe handling of chemicals. The closest of the 25 careers below is Pesticide Handlers, Sprayers, and Applicators, Vegetation, with an 89% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $46,340, or 2% more than the $45,250 pest control workers earn.
why_it_works: A typical day means planning a route, inspecting homes, explaining treatments and handling regulated products safely. O*NET rates time management at 3.5 out of 5 for this job and complex problem solving at 3.25. Hazardous materials, inspection and septic work use the same safety habits. Most matches need no extra schooling. To earn more, you will usually learn to run, install and monitor equipment.
tips: List your state applicator license and any hazmat training; both are valued in inspection and removal jobs.
Fish and Game Wardens earn $74,060, which is 64% more, though most need a certificate or associate degree.
Hazardous Materials Removal Workers earn $49,450, or 9% more, with similar safety rules.

faq.q: What jobs can former pest control workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are vegetation pesticide applicators (89%), Hazardous Materials Removal Workers (83%) and septic tank and sewer pipe cleaners (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Agricultural Inspectors are 74% matched and earn $49,940, which is 10% more than pest control pays.

faq.q: Which careers for pest control workers pay more?
faq.a: 22 of the 25 matches pay more than the $45,250 pest control median. Subway and Streetcar Operators earn $86,380 (91% more), Fish and Game Wardens $74,060 (64% more) and explosives workers and blasters $61,390 (36% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do pest control workers need a degree to switch jobs?
faq.a: Usually not. 20 of the 25 matches need no more education than pest control workers already have. Many jobs in this group expect a professional certification or license instead, which you may already hold through your state applicator license and safety training.

faq.q: What skills should pest control workers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, programming, installation and operations monitoring. Social perceptiveness already rates 3.38 out of 5 for pest control in O*NET, so learning to run and install equipment is the main step.
